To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ang-2 and its receptor VEGFR-2 play a significant role in OSCC and that the combination of these factors may be a better prognostic indicator than each factor alone.
high expression of Ang2 alone or combined with VEGFR3 in OSCC is associated with poor prognosis.

the expression of angiopoietin- 2 (Ang-2) and Vascular Endthelial Growth Factor Recepto 3 (VEGFR-3) in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCC) is upregulated compared to normal oral mucosa, and that high Ang-2 expression is positively correlated with micro-vessel density and high VEGF-R3 expression is positively correlated to lymphatic vessel density and lymph-node metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the role of the VEGF-A and Angiopoietins in the process of lymphangiogenesis and angiogenesis in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and the possible relationship of the expression of these molecules with the prognosis of the disease.
the study of the expression of the Ang-2 and of the VEGFR-2 receptors in the tumor and in the adjacent noncancerous tissues of the patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma.
the role of the Ang-2 and/or VEGFR- 3 expression in the prognosis of OSCC.

the expression of Ang-1, VEGF, VEGFR-2 and VWF was significantly higher in OSCC than in the adjacent non-cancerous tissue.

the expression of Ang-1 and Ang-2 in OSCC is significantly up-regulated compared to normal oral tissue, and that the Ang-2 expression is significantly associated with MVD and VEGFR3 expression is significantly associated LVD.
high Ang-2 expression alone or in combination VEGFR-2 may be a useful prognostic marker in OSCC.

Ang-2 expression may predict survival of OSCC patients.
